Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. Out walks the umpires followed by the players of Sri Lanka. Travis Head comes out at the top for the Aussies and he is accompanied by Matthew Short. Asitha Fernando will open the attack for Sri Lanka.
... The Run Chase ...

Australia on the other hand did not look like the Australian team we have seen in the past. With a few drop catches and fast bowlers providing too much width, it was not easy for Steven Smith to contain the Sri Lankan batters at the crease. They started well in the first 10 overs but the spinners did not capitalize and failed to pick up wickets in the middle overs. Now they stand on a run chase of 281 runs in 50 overs in front of a brilliant spin attack of Sri Lanka. Let's see what goes down in the Second Innings. Stay tuned for the Run Chase!

Sri Lanka started off with the early wicket of Pathum Nissanka. The younster, Nishan Madushka and Kusal Mendis then stitched up a good partnership where Nishan Madushka played the second fiddle and Kusal Mendis took care of the scoring. The youngster made a well-composed half-century and was sent back by a brilliant catch by Adam Zampa at fine leg. Kusal Mendis went on to score his fifth ODI Hundred with a few wickets falling around him till the time, the skipper Charith Asalanka came to the crease. It was then the brilliance of Charith Asalanka to take his team to 281 in 50 overs.

Sri Lanka finished on a high and it's the skipper once again, Charith Asalanka leading his side to a brilliant score of 281/4 on a wicket that has a lot for the spinners. Charith Asalanka walks away not out on 78 and the Australia team has no answers to his batting in this ODI series. With a brilliant hundred from Kusal Mendis after a good start from the youngster Nishan Madushka who scored his 51, Sri Lanka looks ahead in the game after the end of the first innings.

PITCH REPORT! Farveez Maharoof provides insights into the pitch conditions, highlighting another hot and humid day. He notes that the match has shifted from pitch number five to pitch number seven, but the surfaces appear nearly identical. A key difference is the wider cracks, likely due to watering the previous day, while the top remains slightly tacky. Maharoof recalls the unexpected seam movement in the first 18 overs of the last match, particularly when Australia bowled, and mentions that Sri Lanka also managed to extract some movement in the second innings.

Australia captain Steve Smith acknowledges that the pitch looks similar to the previous game and mentions that he would have preferred to bat first but respects the toss outcome. He expresses confidence in his team’s ability to bowl well early and chase effectively later. Smith announces four changes to the playing XI, with Dwarshuis, Head, Maxwell, and Tanvir Sangha coming in. Reflecting on the last match, he stresses the need for better partnerships and bigger scores in the middle order, acknowledging that they fell too far behind in the previous game.

Sri Lanka captain Charith Asalanka confirms that his team will bat first, stating that the pitch looks similar to the previous game. He emphasizes the need to improve their batting and put up a bigger total. Asalanka also announces one change in the playing XI, with Nishan Madushka replacing Avishka Fernando. He expresses confidence in the team, highlighting that the win in the last game has given them momentum heading into this match.

Chasing a modest target of 215, Australia had a nightmare start. Matthew Short fell for a duck on the second ball of the innings leaving Australia in deep trouble. Steve Smith was cleaned up by Wellalage on 12, and Marnus Labuschagne was trapped LBW by Maheesh Theekshana. While Alex Carey fought hard with a 41-run knock, he fell while trying to accelerate, and the visitors never recovered. Australia were bowled out for just 165 in 33.5 overs, falling 49 runs short of the target. Maheesh Theekshana was the star with the ball, finishing with 4/40 in 9.5 overs, while Asitha Fernando and Dunith Wellalage picked up two wickets each. Wanindu Hasaranga and Asalanka also chipped in with one wicket apiece.

Winning the toss and electing to bat, Sri Lanka got off to a disastrous start. Openers Pathum Nissanka and Avishka Fernando were dismissed in the first two overs by Spencer Johnson and Aaron Hardie, leaving the hosts reeling early. Things only got worse when Kusal Mendis, after a few streaky boundaries, edged one behind off Hardie. At 55/5 in the 15th over, Sri Lanka looked set for a total under 150. But captain Charith Asalanka stepped up when it mattered the most. He played a brilliant counter-attacking knock, smashing 127 off 126 balls. Sri Lanka reached 214 before being bowled out in 46 overs. For Australia, Sean Abbott was the pick of the bowlers with 3 wickets, while Hardie, Nathan Ellis, and Johnson picked up two each to wrap up the Sri Lankan innings.

Sri Lanka delivered a commanding performance in the series opener, outclassing a depleted Australian side to take a 1-0 lead in the short two-match ODI series. Charith Asalanka led from the front, playing a sensational 127-run knock and even contributing with the ball, as the hosts secured a 49-run victory in Colombo. The two teams return to the R. Premadasa Stadium for the final match of the series, with Sri Lanka aiming for a clean sweep and Australia desperate to level things up.

We are down to the second and final ODI of the series between Sri Lanka and Australia at the R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo. After going down in the series opener, the tourists will be eager for a quick turnaround to end the series on a high before heading to Pakistan for the Champions Trophy. In the first game, Sri Lankan skipper Charith Asalanka was the difference between the two sides, with his superb century guiding the hosts to a total of 214, which ultimately proved enough for a 49-run victory. Australia’s batting left a lot to be desired, particularly in terms of application, and they will be looking for a much-improved performance. Josh Inglis, Travis Head, and Glenn Maxwell missed the first game but could be given crucial game time ahead of the Champions Trophy. With the ball, the pace quartet of Spencer Johnson, Aaron Hardie, Nathan Ellis, and Sean Abbott impressed, but Adam Zampa struggled to find his rhythm and will be keen to hit his straps. As for Sri Lanka, they do not have an immediate tournament to prepare for, but their top order consisting of Pathum Nissanka, Avishka Fernando, and Kusal Mendis, will be eager to rectify their struggles, particularly in terms of footwork against Australia’s pacers. Wanindu Hasaranga is usually the centre of attention when Sri Lanka take the field, but it was an off day for him in the series opener. Struggling for rhythm, he found himself overshadowed by the performances of fellow spinners Maheesh Theekshana and Dunith Wellalage. He will be eager to bounce back and make a bigger impact in this game. Can Sri Lanka seal a series sweep, or will Australia hit back and gain momentum ahead of the Champions Trophy? We shall find out.
